- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high, then apply mean reversion toward 10–15 day moving average.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.3), model tends to overestimate; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day of positive sentiment.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating +/–0.3), especially if recent price is trending upward; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term mean reversion; if price has moved >10% from 10-day average, adjust forecast to align with 10-day MA within 2–3 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative and price is trending down, model may lag; forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of true trend, but not exceed 3% above recent low.
